p.src: As Jia Yucun was about to cross the river, he saw someone come running at full speed. The man reached him and cried, “My lord, the temple you just visited has caught fire!” Yucun looked back and saw flames blazing into the sky and flying ash obscuring his sight. Yucun thought, “How strange! I have only just left and have not gone far. Where could this fire have come from? Can Shiyin have met with disaster there?” He wanted to go back, but feared delaying his crossing; yet if he did not return, he could not set his mind at ease. After thinking for a moment, he asked, “Did you see that old Taoist come out just now?” The man replied, “I originally followed Your Lordship out, but my stomach began to ache, so I stepped aside for a moment. When I looked back, I saw a great blaze. It turned out that the temple was on fire, so I hurried here especially to report it to Your Lordship. I did not see anyone come out.” Though Yucun remained suspicious, he was ultimately a man whose heart was set on rank and profit; how could he be willing to go back and investigate? He therefore told the man, “Wait here until the fire is out, then go inside and see whether the old Taoist is there. Come and report to me at once.” The man had no choice but to assent and remain there waiting.

p.src: Yucun crossed the river and continued his inspection. After examining several places, he stopped to rest whenever he came to an official lodging house. The next day he travelled another stage and entered the capital gates, where a crowd of runners received him and escorted him with men shouting before and thronging behind. Seated in his sedan chair, Yucun heard a commotion among the men clearing the way ahead. Yucun asked what was happening. One of the men clearing the way dragged someone over, made him kneel before the sedan, and reported, “This fellow was too drunk to move aside and instead came barging into us. When I shouted at him, he used his drunkenness as an excuse to make trouble, lay down in the middle of the street, and claimed that I had beaten him.” Yucun said, “I am the official governing this district. You are all people under my jurisdiction. Knowing that this prefect was passing, you got drunk and failed to stand aside, and now you even dare to make trouble!” The man replied, “I bought my drink with my own money, and when drunk I lay on the Emperor’s ground. Not even a great lord such as yourself has the right to interfere.” Yucun said angrily, “This man has no respect for law or discipline. Ask him his name.” The man answered, “My name is Ni Er, the Drunken Vajra.” This angered Yucun, who ordered his men, “Beat this ‘Vajra’ and let us see whether he truly is one!” His men forced Ni Er to the ground and gave him several hard lashes. The pain sobered Ni Er, and he begged for mercy. Yucun laughed from inside his sedan. “So this is the sort of Vajra you are! I shall stop beating you for now. Take him to the yamen, and there I shall question him at leisure.” The runners acknowledged the order, bound Ni Er, and dragged him away. Ni Er pleaded piteously, but it was no use. Yucun went into the palace to report on his mission and return to his office, giving the incident no further thought.

p.src: The onlookers in the street gathered in twos and threes, saying, “Ni Er relies on his strength and uses drunkenness to extort people. Today he has fallen into Lord Jia’s hands, and I fear he will not be let off lightly.” Word of this soon reached his wife and daughter. When Ni Er still had not returned home that night, his daughter went searching for him at every gambling den. All the gamblers told her the same story, and in her distress she began to weep. Everyone told her, “There is no need to worry. Lord Jia belongs to the same clan as the Rong Mansion. Some Second Master in the Rong Mansion is friendly with your father. Go with your mother and ask him to intercede, and your father will be released.” Hearing this, Ni Er’s daughter thought, “Indeed, Father often says that Second Master Jia next door is a good friend of his. Why should we not go and seek his help?” She hurried home and told her mother at once. Mother and daughter went to seek out Jia Yun.

p.src: Jia Yun happened to be at home that day. When he saw the mother and daughter arrive, he invited them to sit down. Jia Yun’s mother poured them tea. Ni Er’s wife and daughter related how Lord Jia had arrested him and pleaded, “We beg Second Master to intercede and have him released.” Jia Yun agreed at once, saying, “That is nothing. I need only speak a word at the West Mansion, and he will be released. Lord Jia owes his rise to such high office entirely to our West Mansion. All that is needed is to send someone with a message, and the matter will be settled.” Delighted, Ni Er’s wife and daughter went back to the yamen and told him not to worry: they had already appealed to Second Master Jia, who had readily promised that Ni Er would be released once he interceded. Ni Er was pleased to hear this as well.

p.src: Unexpectedly, ever since the day when Xifeng refused the gift Jia Yun had brought her, he had felt too embarrassed to enter and seldom visited the Rong Mansion. The gatekeepers of the Rong Mansion always took their cue from their masters. If their masters favored someone and encouraged his visits, they treated him with some respect and announced him as soon as he arrived; but if their masters paid him little heed, they would report no visitor at all, even if he was a kinsman of the family, and simply send him away. That day Jia Yun went to the mansion and said, “I have come to pay my respects to Second Master Lian.” The gatekeepers said, “Second Master is not at home. When he returns, we shall convey your respects for you.” Jia Yun wanted to say that he had also come to pay his respects to Second Mistress, but fearing that the gatekeepers would become impatient, he had no choice but to go home. Then Ni Er’s wife and daughter pressed him, saying, “Second Master is always telling us that, no matter which yamen it may be, no one would dare refuse a word from your mansion. Now this official even belongs to the same clan, and the matter is nothing serious. If you cannot obtain even this favor, then we have called you Second Master for nothing.” Unable to save face, Jia Yun continued to speak boastfully: “We had business at home yesterday, so I did not send anyone with the message. But once it is delivered today, he is certain to be released. What is so difficult about that?” Ni Er’s wife and daughter had no choice but to believe him.

p.src: Little did Jia Yun know that lately he would not even be admitted through the main gate. He went around to the rear, intending to enter the garden and find Baoyu, but the garden gate was locked, so he could only return crestfallen. He recalled, “That year Ni Er lent me money. I bought perfume and gave it to him, and only then was I assigned the tree-planting job. Now that I have no money with which to grease his palm, he turns me away. He is no good man either. He takes the clan funds left by the old master and lends them outside at ten percent interest, yet when impoverished members of his own clan wish to borrow even one tael, he refuses them. He imagines he can remain prosperous all his life, but little does he know how foul his reputation has become outside. I shall hold my tongue, but if I began to speak, who knows how many murder cases I could tell of!” Thinking thus, he reached home and found Ni Er's wife and daughter waiting for him. Jia Yun had no answer to give them, so he said, “The western mansion has already sent word that His Excellency Jia will not consent. Your best hope is to appeal to Leng Zixing, a relative of Zhou Rui, a servant in our household.” Ni Er's wife and daughter replied, “If even a respectable gentleman like you, Second Master, is of no use, a servant will surely be still less use.” Embarrassed and growing anxious, Jia Yun said, “You do not understand. These days servants are far more powerful than their masters.” Seeing that nothing could be done, Ni Er's wife and daughter merely gave a few cold laughs and said, “We are sorry to have put you to the trouble of running about in vain these past few days, Second Master. When our man comes out, we shall have him thank you properly.” With that they left and asked someone else to secure Ni Er's release. He had received only a few strokes of the board and was guilty of no serious offense.

p.src: When Ni Er returned home, his wife and daughter told him everything about the Jia family's refusal to intercede. Ni Er was drinking at the time. Enraged, he wanted to go after Jia Yun and cried, “That little bastard, that heartless wretch! At first, when he had nothing to eat and wanted to worm his way into the mansion to obtain employment, it was only thanks to Master Ni Er that he received help. Now that I am in trouble, he will do nothing for me. Very well! If I, Ni Er, raise a commotion, neither of the two mansions will come out of it clean!” His wife and daughter hastily tried to restrain him. “Oh, whenever you have swallowed that yellow brew, you start raving as if there were neither heaven nor sun! Was it not drunken disorder that got you into trouble the other day? The beating you took has not even healed, and here you are making trouble again.” Ni Er said, “Do you think a beating will make me afraid of them? All I need is a pretext! While I was in prison, I made the acquaintance of several loyal and honorable fellows. From what I heard them say, there are many people surnamed Jia not only in the capital but also in the provinces. The other day, several servants of a Jia family were brought into the prison. I said that although the younger generation and the servants of the Jia family here were no good, their elders were decent, so how could they have committed a crime? After making inquiries, I learned that they belonged to the same clan as the Jia family here but all lived in the provinces. Their cases had been tried and settled, and they had been escorted to the capital for punishment. Only then was I relieved. But since young Jia the Second has proved ungrateful and faithless, I shall tell my friends how his family abuses its power to bully others, how it squeezes the common people, and how it forcibly takes married women from their husbands. I shall have them raise an outcry. Once word reaches the ears of the chief magistrate and the uproar begins, then you will learn what sort of Vajra Ni Er really is!” His wife said, “You have been drinking; go to sleep! Whose wife has he ever seized? Do not babble about things that never happened.” Ni Er said, “You stay at home; what could you know of affairs outside? The year before last, I ran into young Zhang at a gambling house. He said the Jia family had taken his woman and even consulted me about it. It was I who advised him to let the matter drop. But I wonder where young Zhang has gone now; I have not seen him these past two years. If I run into him, I, Ni Er, shall devise a scheme to ruin Jia the Second and make him pay handsome tribute to his grand master Ni Er before I let the matter rest. And now you dare ignore me!” With that he flung himself down. He continued muttering for a while, then fell asleep. His wife and daughter took his words for drunken rambling and paid him no heed. Early the next morning, Ni Er went off to the gambling house again. But no more of this for now.

p.src: Meanwhile, Yucun returned home and rested for the night. He told his wife all about encountering Zhen Shiyin on the road. His wife reproached him: “Why did you not go back to see what had happened? If he was burned to death, would that not make us utterly heartless?” As she spoke, tears fell from her eyes. Yucun said, “He has left the secular world behind and would not consent to live with us.” While they were speaking, a message came in from outside: “The man whom Your Excellency ordered the other day to inspect the temple fire has returned to make his report.” Yucun strolled out. The constable bent one knee in salutation and reported, “In obedience to Your Excellency's command, I went back. Without even waiting for the fire to die down, I braved the flames and entered to look for that Taoist, only to find that the place where he had been sitting was almost entirely burned away. I thought the Taoist must surely have burned to death. The burning walls and rooms had collapsed backward, yet there was not a trace of the Taoist. Only a meditation mat and a gourd dipper remained perfectly intact. I searched everywhere for his corpse, but could not find so much as a fragment of bone. Fearing that Your Excellency might not believe me, I meant to bring back the mat and the dipper as proof. But the moment I touched them, they both turned to ashes.” When Yucun had heard the report, he understood in his heart that Shiyin had ascended to immortality, and he dismissed the constable. On returning to his room, he said nothing of Shiyin's immolation, fearing that his wife, unable to understand, would merely be overcome by grief. He told her only that no trace of Shiyin had been found and that he must have left before the fire.

p.src: After Yucun came out, he sat alone in his study and was just about to ponder Shiyin’s words when a servant suddenly reported, “An edict has come from the Inner Court ordering you to examine a case.” Yucun hurried into his sedan chair and proceeded to the palace, where he heard someone say, “Jia Cunzhou, the Grain Intendant of Jiangxi, was impeached and recalled today and is now at court confessing his fault.” Yucun hastened to the Grand Secretariat, greeted the senior officials, and read the edict concerning the mishandling of affairs along the coast. On coming out, he immediately sought out Jia Zheng, first uttered a few words of indignation on his behalf, then congratulated him and asked, “Did you have a good journey?” Jia Zheng gave him a detailed account of all that had happened since their parting. Yucun asked, “Have you submitted your memorial confessing fault?” “It has already been submitted,” replied Jia Zheng. “I shall wait until after the imperial meal and see what edict comes down.” While they were speaking, an imperial summons for Jia Zheng was relayed from within, and he hurried inside. All the senior officials who were concerned for Jia Zheng remained inside to await him. Only after a long while did Jia Zheng emerge, his brow streaming with sweat. They went forward to meet him and asked, “What did His Majesty say?” Jia Zheng stuck out his tongue and exclaimed, “It frightened me to death—frightened me to death! I am grateful for your concern, gentlemen; fortunately, nothing happened.” They asked, “What did His Majesty question you about?” Jia Zheng replied, “His Majesty asked about the case of firearms being smuggled through Yunnan. The memorial stated that the culprit was a servant of Jia Hua, the former Grand Preceptor. His Majesty had always remembered the name of our ancestor, and so he questioned me about it. I hurriedly kowtowed and reported that our ancestor’s name was Daihua. His Majesty smiled and said, ‘Was not the man formerly appointed to the Ministry of War and later demoted to Prefect also called Jia Hua?’” Yucun, who was standing nearby, was startled by this and asked Jia Zheng, “What answer did you make, sir?” Jia Zheng replied, “I answered slowly, ‘Jia Hua, the former Grand Preceptor, was a native of Yunnan; the present Prefect, Jia So-and-so, is a native of Zhejiang.’ His Majesty then asked, ‘Is Jia Fan, against whom the Prefect of Suzhou has memorialized, a member of your clan?’ I kowtowed again and answered, ‘He is.’ His Majesty’s expression changed, and he said, ‘How can you permit a household slave to seize the wives and daughters of respectable commoners by force?’ I dared not utter a word in reply. His Majesty asked again, ‘How is Jia Fan related to you?’ I hastily answered, ‘He is a distant clansman.’ His Majesty grunted and ordered me to withdraw. Was that not an extraordinary thing!” The others said, “It was indeed a remarkable coincidence. How could these two affairs follow one upon the other?” Jia Zheng said, “The affairs themselves are not so strange; the trouble is that all those involved bear the surname Jia. Our humble clan is numerous, after all, and over the many generations it has branched into every sort of family. Though nothing has happened for the moment, it is still unfortunate that His Majesty has taken note of the name ‘Jia.’”

Jia Zheng said, “The affairs themselves are not so strange; the trouble is that all those involved bear the surname Jia.
Our humble clan is numerous, after all, and over the many generations it has branched into every sort of family.
Though nothing has happened for the moment, it is still unfortunate that His Majesty has taken note of the name ‘Jia.’”

p.src: The others said, “What is true is true, and what is false is false. What is there to fear?” Jia Zheng said, “In my heart, I long to leave official life, but I dare not request retirement. Our family now holds two hereditary titles, and there is nothing to be done about that.” Yucun said, “You are still attached to the Ministry of Works, sir. I should think that an official serving in the capital has nothing to fear.” Jia Zheng replied, “Though service in the capital may be safe, I have held provincial office twice, so there is no telling what may happen.” The others said, “We all admire Second Master’s character and conduct. Your elder brother, the First Master, is likewise a good man. You need only keep a stricter hand over the younger generation of your nephews.” Jia Zheng said, “Since I have spent little time at home, I have not looked closely into my nephews’ affairs, and I have not felt altogether easy about them. Since you gentlemen, all of you my closest friends, have raised the matter today, have you perhaps heard that my nephews in the eastern mansion have been behaving improperly?” They replied, “We have heard nothing else, except that several vice-ministers are not on very good terms, and there is some discontent among the palace eunuchs as well. There should be little to fear, but you ought to caution your nephews over there to take care in everything they do.” Having said this, they raised their hands in farewell and dispersed.

p.src: Jia Zheng then returned home. All his sons, nephews, and the rest came forward to welcome him. Jia Zheng went first to pay his respects to Grandmother Jia; then all the sons and nephews paid their respects to him, and together they entered the mansion. Lady Wang and the others had already reached the Hall of Glorious Felicity to welcome him. Jia Zheng first went to Grandmother Jia’s quarters to pay his respects and spoke of matters that had occurred during their separation. Grandmother Jia asked for news of Tanchun. Jia Zheng reported the full particulars of her betrothal and added, “Your son had to depart in such haste that I could not remain past the Double Ninth Festival. Though I did not see her myself, I heard from the family into which she married that everything was exceedingly well. Her father-in-law and mother-in-law both sent their respects to you and Father. They also said they would probably be transferred back to the capital sometime this winter or next spring. That would be a happy outcome. But now that we hear trouble has broken out along the coast, I fear the transfer may still be impossible by then.” At first, Grandmother Jia had been distressed because Jia Zheng had returned after being demoted and transferred, while Tanchun was far away in a strange land without a single relative or old acquaintance nearby; but after Jia Zheng explained the official circumstances and assured her that Tanchun was well, her sorrow turned to joy, and with a smile she told him to go out. The brothers then met, and all the sons and nephews paid their respects; it was settled that they would worship at the ancestral hall early the following morning.

p.src: Jia Zheng returned to his own rooms, where Lady Wang and the others came to greet him, followed by Baoyu and Jia Lian, who paid their respects separately. Jia Zheng saw that Baoyu’s face was indeed fuller than when he had left and that he seemed calmer. Unaware of the confusion in his mind, he was delighted and gave no thought to his own demotion, reflecting that the old lady had fortunately managed matters well. Seeing too that Baochai was steadier and more composed than ever, and that young Lan was refined and handsome, his pleasure showed plainly on his face. Only Huan was just as he had always been, and Jia Zheng still felt little affection for him. After resting for quite a while, he suddenly asked, “Why is one person missing today?” Lady Wang knew he was thinking of Daiyu. Since she had not mentioned the matter in her letters, and he had only just arrived home in such high spirits, she thought it best not to tell him outright and merely said that Daiyu was ill. Little did she know that Baoyu’s heart already felt as though knives were churning within it; only because his father had returned did he master himself and remain in attendance. Lady Wang laid a banquet to welcome Jia Zheng home, and his children and grandchildren offered him wine. Although Xifeng was only his nephew’s wife, she was now managing the household, so she too offered him wine along with Baochai and the others. After Jia Zheng had ordered one round of wine served, he said, “You may all go and rest.” He told the household servants that they need not attend him and should present themselves only after he had worshipped at the ancestral shrine the following morning. Once these arrangements were settled, Jia Zheng and Lady Wang spoke of events since their parting, though there were many other matters that she dared not mention. It was Jia Zheng himself who first brought up Wang Ziteng, and even then Lady Wang dared not give way to grief. When Jia Zheng next spoke of Pan, Lady Wang merely said that he had brought his troubles upon himself; and, taking the opportunity, she also told him that Daiyu had died. Jia Zheng was taken completely aback. Tears fell from his eyes, and he sighed again and again. Lady Wang could no longer contain herself and began to weep as well. Caiyun and the other maids beside her hurriedly tugged at her clothes. Lady Wang checked her tears, spoke once more of happier things, and then they retired for the night.

p.src: Early the next morning, Jia Zheng went to perform the rites at the ancestral shrine, accompanied by all the younger men of the family. Jia Zheng then seated himself in a side room beside the shrine, summoned Jia Zhen and Jia Lian, and questioned them about the affairs of the household. Jia Zhen told him only what could safely be told. Jia Zheng said, “I have only just returned, so it would not be proper for me to question you closely. But I have heard people outside say that your household is even less what it once was, so you must exercise caution in everything. You are no longer young. You should discipline the children and not let them offend people outside. Lian, you should heed this too. I am not reprimanding you the moment I arrive home; I speak only because certain things have reached my ears. You must be all the more careful.” Jia Zhen and the others flushed crimson and merely answered, “Yes,” not daring to say anything more. Jia Zheng let the matter rest there. On returning to the western mansion, he received the kowtows of all the household servants, then went inside again, where the maidservants paid their respects; there is no need to dwell on the details.

p.src: As for Baoyu, when Jia Zheng had asked about Daiyu the previous day and Lady Wang had replied that she was ill, he had grieved in secret. He held out until Jia Zheng dismissed him, but on the way back he shed many tears. When he returned to his rooms, he found Baochai talking with Xiren and the others, so he sat alone in the outer room, brooding. Baochai told Xiren to take him some tea. Supposing that he was distressed because he feared his father would question him about his studies, she had no choice but to come over and console him. Taking advantage of this, Baoyu went over to Baochai and said, “You go to bed first tonight. I need to compose myself. My memory is worse now than ever; for every three words I say, I forget two, and Father will not like the look of that. You go to sleep and let Xiren sit with me for a while.” Baochai did not think it proper to press him and nodded her assent.

p.src: When Baoyu came out, he spoke softly to Xiren and pleaded, “Ask Zijuan to come here. I have something to ask her. But whenever Zijuan sees me, resentment shows on her face, so you must first soothe her anger and reason with her before bringing her here.” Xiren said, “I was glad when you said you wanted to compose yourself, but how have you ended up fixing your thoughts on this again? Can whatever you have to ask not wait until tomorrow?” Baoyu said, “Tonight is the only time I have free. If Father orders me to do something tomorrow, I shall have no time. Dear sister, please hurry and fetch her.” Xiren said, “She will not come unless the young mistress sends for her.” “That is precisely why you must go and explain matters to her,” said Baoyu. “And what am I to tell her?” asked Xiren. Baoyu said, “Do you still not understand what is in my heart and hers? It is all because of Miss Lin. Tell her I was never faithless; it is all of you who have made me appear a faithless man!” As he spoke, he glanced toward the inner room, pointed with his hand, and said, “I never wanted her in the first place. It was all a trick played on me by the old lady and the others. They took a perfectly healthy Miss Lin and brought about her death. Even if she had to die, they should at least have let me see her and explain everything clearly, so that she could die without blaming me. After all, you heard Third Sister and the others say that she resented me as she lay dying. And Zijuan, for her young mistress’s sake, hates me bitterly too. Do you think I am a heartless man? Qingwen was, after all, only a maid and had no extraordinary virtues, yet when she died—I may as well tell you the truth—I even composed a funeral elegy for her. Miss Lin saw that with her own eyes. Now that Miss Lin is dead, can she possibly mean less to me than Qingwen? I cannot even hold a single offering for her. Besides, Miss Lin’s spirit must still possess divine awareness after death; when she thinks of this, will she not blame me all the more?” Xiren said, “If you want to make an offering, then go and do it. Who is stopping you?” Baoyu said, “Ever since I recovered, I have wanted to compose a funeral elegy for her, but I do not know why not the slightest inspiration comes to me now. For someone else, something dashed off carelessly might suffice, but an elegy for her must not contain the least trace of coarseness. That is why I want Zijuan to come, so that I may ask how she discerned her young mistress’s feelings. Before I fell ill, I could still remember it, but since my illness I have forgotten everything. You told me that Miss Lin had already recovered, so how did she come to die so suddenly? When she was well and I did not go to see her, what did she say? And when I was ill and she did not come, what did she say then? As for all her belongings, I coaxed you into bringing them here, but your young mistress will never allow anyone to touch them. I cannot think what she means by it.” Xiren said, “The young mistress merely fears that you will be distressed. What else could it mean?”

p.src: Baoyu said, “I don’t believe it. If Miss Lin truly cared for me, why did she burn her poetry manuscripts as she lay dying instead of leaving them to me as a keepsake? And I heard that music sounded in the heavens; she must have become a divine being or ascended to immortality. Although I saw the coffin, I still do not know whether she was really inside it.” Xiren said, “You are talking more and more foolishly. How could someone who had not died be put into a coffin and treated as dead?” Baoyu said, “No, that isn’t what I mean! Those who become immortals may depart in the flesh, or they may cast off their mortal shell. Dear sister, please send for Zijuan after all.” Xiren said, “Let me first explain carefully what is troubling you. If she agrees to come, all will be well, but if she refuses, it will take no end of persuasion; and even if she comes, she will not tell you everything to your face. This is what I think: tomorrow, after Second Mistress has gone upstairs, I will question her at leisure; perhaps then I can learn the details. When I find a free moment, I will tell you everything at leisure.” Baoyu said, “What you say makes sense, but you have no idea how anxious I feel.”

p.src: As they were speaking, Sheyue came out and said, “Second Mistress says it is already the fourth watch and asks Second Master to go in and sleep. Sister Xiren must have become so absorbed in talking that she has forgotten the hour.” Hearing this, Xiren said, “Indeed, it is time for bed. Let us continue our talk tomorrow.” Baoyu had no choice but to go inside, though he whispered once more in Xiren’s ear, “Whatever you do, don’t forget tomorrow.” Xiren smiled. “I know.” Sheyue pulled a face and laughed. “You two are plotting something mysterious again. Why not explain it to Second Mistress and simply go sleep in Xiren’s room? Then you can talk all night, and the rest of us won’t interfere.” Baoyu waved his hand. “Say no more.” Xiren snapped, “You little hussy, there you go wagging your tongue again! Just wait—I’ll tear your mouth tomorrow!” Then she turned to Baoyu and said, “See what trouble you have caused? You have kept me talking until the fourth watch.” Still speaking, she escorted Baoyu into his room, and then they all dispersed.

p.src: Baoyu did not sleep that night, and the next day he was still thinking about the matter. Then word was passed in from outside: “Because Master has returned home, all his relatives and friends wish to sponsor a theatrical performance to welcome him back. Master repeatedly declined, saying that there was no need for a performance; instead, he would prepare some simple food and wine at home and invite his relatives and friends over for a pleasant talk. A banquet has therefore been set for the day after tomorrow, and we have come in to report it.” Who the guests were remains unknown; the next chapter will reveal it.
